alternative_scenarios.name: Recommended launch
alternative_scenarios.rationale: Reconciled market value; balances absorption speed and captured value. Default: price at comps and negotiate from strength.

alternative_scenarios.name: Premium launch
alternative_scenarios.rationale: Top of the evidenced range; leans on the future-signal story (development score 0.0). Enables the 'raise later, never cut' strategy under strong demand.

Zarqa.narrative: For a high apartment in Zarqa (~175 m²), the recommended launch price is 303 JD/m², within a defensible range of 197–410 JD/m² (confidence: L, 0.43; 80% interval 197–410). This is anchored on 11 comparable listing(s), each normalised to the subject with market-derived adjustments and calibrated from asking to transaction level; comps needing fewer/smaller adjustments carried more weight. Cross-checks: cost floor ≈ 155, income ceiling ≈ 248. Convergence supports the estimate; divergence is captured in the risks. Key risk: furnishing not supplied — those premiums could not be applied.

evidence_objects.method: documented assumption: asking prices sit 5–15% above transactions (client PDF)

sources.name: Client methodology PDF — Real Estate Pricing Strategies

evidence_objects.explanation: Portal prices are asking prices, not sales. A documented 5–15% gap is applied to estimate the transaction level.

evidence_objects.method: Value = replacement construction cost − depreciation (new-build ≈ 0)
evidence_objects.explanation: A rational buyer will not pay below the cost to rebuild: standard construction ≈ 155 JD/m². This sets the minimum-safe price.

evidence_objects.method: income approach: annual rent ÷ derived market yield (8.9%, citywide rents vs sales)
evidence_objects.explanation: Investment buyers cap price at rent ÷ required yield (8.9%). Above ≈ 856 JD/m² the unit stops clearing to investors.

evidence_objects.method: seller-type share of the 12 comps
evidence_objects.explanation: Of the comparables driving this estimate, 100% agent-listed — a predominantly agency-brokered comp set. Provided as market texture; it does not move the price.

risk_factors.detail: furnishing not supplied — those premiums could not be applied.
Comparison, cost and income approaches disagree (PDF: divergence is informative).
Widen the range and gather more evidence before committing.
Bayut/OpenSooq do not expose view per listing — the view/aspect factor will attach at neighborhood level from qualitative research (R7), not per comp.
Listings are almost entirely 'covered' parking with too few usable 'open'/'none' rows to form a paired differential — parking is not adjusted.
Elevator, Finish quality too sparse to derive even citywide — not adjusted.
CBJ index covers only through none; time-adjustment of stale comps is disabled rather than extrapolated.
No infrastructure/development items collected yet — the appreciation story is not evidenced; premium tier rests on the comparison band.
